short: A decisive Theban victory that shattered Sparta's aura of military invincibility and ended Spartan hegemony.
full:
In July 371 BCE, a Spartan army marched into Boeotia to force the city-state of Thebes to dissolve its regional league. At the Battle of Leuctra, the Theban commander Epaminondas employed a revolutionary tactical innovation. He massed his best troops in a deep column on his left wing—traditionally the weaker side in Greek warfare—to directly strike the elite Spartan guard. The sheer weight and momentum of the Theban formation broke the Spartan line.

The battle resulted in the death of the Spartan king Cleombrotus I and hundreds of elite Spartiates, losses from which Spartan manpower would never recover. This crushing defeat ended Spartan dominance over mainland Greece and inaugurated a brief period of Theban hegemony, fundamentally altering the balance of power before the rise of Macedon.
